key_insight: ZAGNet improves patient-level lung ultrasound diagnosis by modeling anatomical zone relationships with a graph network instead of using simple pooling across scans.
clinical_relevance: This could make automated LUS assessment more robust in real-world exams where some zones are missing or scanned inconsistently.
method: Represents tracked pathology findings as graph nodes linked by lung-zone adjacency.
Uses a graph transformer plus a virtual global node to aggregate patient-level predictions.
Trains with only patient-level labels for consolidation and pleural effusion.
evidence_signal: In 714 subjects and 20,256 LUS video loops, ZAGNet achieved AUCs of 0.803 for consolidation and 0.893 for pleural effusion, outperforming max and mean pooling baselines.
watch_item: Performance was shown on a retrospective multicenter dataset, so prospective validation and workflow integration are still needed before clinical use.
paper_title: ZAGNet: Zone-Aware Graph Aggregation Network for Patient-Level Lung Ultrasound Diagnosis
